page: Microsoft Azure D64nds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 64 dedicated virtual cores based on the x86_64 Intel processor architecture, paired with 256.0 GB of system memory. This yields a standard balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, suiting environments that demand proportional memory and processing capability without leaning heavily toward memory or compute extremes.

A primary hardware differentiator for the D64nds_v6 instance is its inclusion of 3,780 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. Unlike diskless virtual machines, the onboard NVMe disk offers direct high-throughput and low-latency ephemeral scratch space. The instance does not include discrete hardware accelerators, maintaining a zero GPU configuration, and provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on virtual network routing for external connectivity.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, bundling 3,780 GB of fast local NVMe capacity eliminates the need to provision equivalent ephemeral tiers via external attached block storage. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent compute performance under continuous load. Tradeoffs include the volatile nature of local NVMe storage, requiring stateful architectures to replicate persistent data elsewhere.

Microsoft Azure D64nds_v6 is engineered for scale-out transactional databases, high-capacity caching nodes, search engine indexing, batch processing, continuous integration build servers, and web application tiers requiring substantial temporary local scratch space.

Qualitative cost efficiency is driven by the pre-allocated high-capacity local disk, reducing reliance on auxiliary managed disks for volatile workloads. Due to its balanced resource footprint and fast local storage tier, the D64nds_v6 is suited for large relational databases, distributed caching layers, enterprise application hosting, and intensive continuous integration pipelines.
